name: QUANTUM Trails
description: Step beyond the visible and into the world of QUANTUM. Join our Mediators, Ajay and Apoorva, as they trace the connections between science, art and imagination. Discover the stories and ideas behind the works and experience the many strange, playful and thought-provoking ways quantum phenomena come to life.

name: The Playful Writer: What Anne Carson Taught Me
description:
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature went to Anne Carson. 

Join Srilata Krishnan for a talk about Carson’s work and what writers and artists can learn from it. Carson’s training was in the classics, which spurred in her a wide-ranging interest in comparative literature, anthropology, history and the arts. Hers is a quintessentially interdisciplinary mind, and her work feels like jewels studded with the gemstones of ancient Greek and Latin literature (Sappho, Catullus, Stesichorus, for instance) and of writers such as Virginia Woolf, Keats and Gertrude Stein.

Formally, her work may be best described as cross-genre. It is the spirit of playfulness and enquiry that drives all of Carson’s work, making each of her books different from the others. Her playfulness precludes neither depth nor rigour, as borne out by every single work of hers. 

As a writer, Srilata has learnt a lot about craft from Carson and will be sharing the subtle ways in which reading Carson helped shape her own writing.

This lecture is organised in collaboration with Infosys Science Foundation.

name: Back to School: We Make the Rules
description:
What if science didn't have to fit neatly into physics, chemistry, and biology? What if you could rewrite the textbook and decide how science should be explored?

This Children's Day, we're going back to school, but this time, you get to write the textbook! In this hands-on workshop, we'll explore surprising connections between things that seem completely unrelated, from everyday experiences to the world of quantum physics. You'll create your own science textbook filled with curious questions, fun experiments, unexpected facts, and a little imagination.

name: Macroeconomic Stabilisation
description:
The 2026 Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences went to researchers Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford for their research on microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation.

Join Chetan Ghate for a lecture reviewing the body of work by the laureates that led to them being awarded the prize in this area. The discussion will explore the relevance of their work in macroeconomic policy making as well as its importance in shaping macroeconomic policy frameworks for India. Be sure to attend this insightful session to learn more and to ask Chetan questions about his own work.

name: The Quantum Art Experiment
description:
What happens when quantum physics meets doodles, wild ideas, and a little bit of creative chaos?

Come find out! Join Divya Chalapathi for a session on mixing art and quantum curiosity through playful drawing experiments, unexpected twists, geometric patterns, and imaginative creations. Explore chance, possibilities, and connections as you create, exchange ideas, and let your imagination run wild. 

No drawing skills or quantum knowledge needed—just bring your curiosity! And the best part? You'll leave with your very own artwork to take home.

name: Namma Oota: Day 1
description:
The Namma Oota festival, hosted by Science Gallery Bengaluru, fuses art, science, and gastronomy.

From what grows in our fields to what lands on our plates, food connects us to questions of ecology, health, culture, and innovation. In the fourth edition of Namma Oota, we hope to explore these curiosities in relation to our diets, communities, and the Anthropocene.

Join us to enjoy the food stalls as we create a flea market-esque ambience with workshops, performances, interactive demonstrations and an open mic to explore. The portico will come alive with the sizzle of tawas, buzzing conversation, and a bit of organised chaos. The festival is curated as a platform to spark conversations and connections on Bengaluru, Oota (food), and sustainability.

name: Heat and Electron Transport: Quantum Signatures
description: The transport properties of materials is a question of fundamental interest to scientists as well as engineers. Some basic questions are: how good is a material for transporting energy and electricity from one region to another? and; can we predict the transport properties of a given material if we are given all the microscopic details of the constituent atoms? Join Abhishek Dhar as he answers these question and describes the role of quantum mechanics in transport theory along with the surprises it throws.

name: Atoms at Work: Building India's First Neutral-Atom Quantum Computer
description: Join Sagar Sutradhar and Nilanjan Kundu for an exclusive visit to QuMiX Lab, the neutral-atom quantum mixture laboratory, headed by Saptarishi Chaudhuri at Raman Research Institute. Discover how India's first neutral-atom quantum computer is taking shape, explore active quantum mixture experiments, and attend researcher-led mini-talks offering a rare, close-up look at the technology and physics driving the National Quantum Mission.

name: Open Mic @ Namma Oota
description:
Join us for an open mic where storytellers, musicians, comedians, poets and singers come together to celebrate the magic of flavours and melodies. We have a vibrant lineup for the evening, spanning everything from a stand-up act starring a man who stands trial for loving Indo-Chinese food to a spoken word performance by a life sciences scholar. 

If this sounds like your jam, we have open mic spots up for grabs on the day. Whether it’s a nostalgia-soaked recipe, a comical culinary mishap, or a poem about unlikely flavour combinations, this is your opportunity to take the stage and share your love of food with a passionate audience. 

The mic is yours!

name: Spill the Beans: A Namma Ooru Food Quiz
description:
Why is Bengaluru named after beans? What chillies are famously used in the perfectly _kara_ Mysuru Masala Dose? What does Rava Idli have to do with World War II?

Bengaluru has plenty of food stories simmering beneath the surface, join Quizmaster Arul Mani for a quiz about the food lore of Namma Ooru.

The quiz will be played in teams of 2–3. Come along with friends or show up solo, and we'll help you find a team.

name: The Journey Along the Memory Lane—spinning my way
description:
Information storage has been around for thousands of years–initially as cave paintings and carvings. Over the millennia it was done on stone, wood, ceramic and eventually on to paper. The seismic shift took place in the 20th century as it moved onto magnetic tapes, discs revolutionising the data storage and communication. 

With the explosion of information generated, and the demand for ever increasing data storage capacity, accompanied by escalating energy needs puts severe strain on energy infrastructure and environment. A potential direction could be via utilising the exotic properties of superconductors to advance future storage and computing technology—a way forward for lower energy operation while reducing our footprint on nature. 

Join Jagadeesh S. Moodera for the talk, in which he will touch upon his journey along the memory path during his years of fundamental scientific research highlighting the evolution of magnetic data storage. The talk will lead you over his years of evolution in this field—how curiosity and quest for knowledge led to the present, and perhaps into the future.

name: Taste, Camera, Action!
description:
We are accustomed to photographing food, carefully composing images of what we eat. But what happens when food becomes the photographer, and we become its subjects?

Taste, Camera, Action! is a playful, participatory workshop that explores how food influences our expressions, gestures and behaviour. Taking inspiration from theatre and improvisation, the workshop invites participants to become actors whose characters are shaped by food. Through tasting, photographing, character creation and performance, participants explore the relationship between sensory experiences and bodily expression.

This workshop is designed by Whatifduo, a new media design practice founded by Mantej and Priyanka.

name: Strange Loop x Tarang Joseph
description: In this set, guitarist Adesh Vinod and singer-songwriter Tarang Joseph build music from scratch, layering guitar riffs, basslines, beats, keys and vocals using electronic music equipment. Drawing on soul and R&B, with influences from artists like Stevie Wonder, Daniel Caesar, Frank Ocean, and Kaytranada, the duo blends live instrumentation with electronic sounds to create something entirely their own. Because it's all looped live, no two sets come out quite the same!

name: Design an Intergalactic Menu
description:
The universe is ending, but dinner must go on! 

In this playful, collaborative workshop by Book-A-Table, step into the role of intergalactic restaurateurs. Inspired by Douglas Adams’ The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy, you are challenged to design a menu for the legendary Restaurant at the End of the Universe.

Equipped with ingredient cards, teams will create a five-course, zero-waste tasting menu with a signature cocktail. Expect improbable combinations, extravagant menu descriptions and a surprise challenge from Mission Control! 

Pitch your culinary creations to the room: How creative is your menu? Have you found use for every ingredient? And, most importantly, does it sound delicious?

There’s no fancy cooking, just imagination, ingenuity and a healthy appetite for the absurd!
